what_agreement_means: two implementations written from the spec in different languages, sharing no code, reach the same verdict on every vector. One implementation passing its own tests is not evidence.
divergence_this_found: Python deserialised a repeated dual member set into a dict (last value wins) while the JavaScript summed the array: objective 2.0 and ACCEPT against 2.4 and refuse, on identical bytes. Neither reading was right; both now refuse, and the case is a permanent vector.
why_mostly_refusals: a suite where everything verifies would not notice a checker that accepts everything -- the failure that matters, since such a checker is worthless and looks perfect
harness_can_fail: proven: corrupting one dual value drops the count (tests/test_cert_conformance.py)
